text:
ella: Hey folks, just opened my first PR to add feature-flag gating for the async export (branch feat/exports/async-flag). Quick orientation Qs: do we prefer a single squashed commit or keep the iterative commits? Also what do you want in the PR body for rollout notes?

frank: Welcome Ella! :wave: For history hygiene we like a tidy main, so squash before merge for small features. If your branch has meaningful intermediate commits (experiments, prototype -> final), keep them while iterating but squash into a single logical commit before final merge.

frank: For the PR body include: ticket link, one-line summary, how to test locally, rollout strategy (feature-flag name + owner), and any perf/regression risks. Example header: "EXPORTS-98: gated async export behind flag exports.async_v2"

ella: Thanks. Our repo uses a monorepo layout with a couple of subpackages; I changed code in core/ and web/. Anything extra I should do for change footprint?

frank: Call out cross-package impacts in the PR. Add a short "Touched areas" section. Also run `make healthy` at repo root which runs quick smoke, lint, and typecheck across packages. If you change public types, add a note under "API compatibility".

ella: Pre-commit flagged a lot of import reorders. Is it ok to include those formatting-only edits in the same commit?

frank: Prefer separating formatting into `chore(format): apply black/ruff/isort` commit so reviewers can focus on logic. If it's a tiny PR, you can squash them together, but separate is clearer.

eng-oncall: Quick CI note: we gate merges on ci/lint, ci/unit, ci/e2e. The e2e job runs in the merge queue; if e2e flakes, use the label `ci-retry` and include the failing job URL.

ella: What about force-pushes during review? I rebased earlier to pick up main changes.

frank: Force-pushes are okay before you request reviewers. Once reviewers are requested, avoid rewriting history unless you call it out. If you must rebase after reviews, use `--force-with-lease` and leave a summary comment describing the rebase and any important diffs. If the rebase is substantial, re-request review.

ella: Any specific review checklist folks expect?

frank: Short checklist in the PR body is great:
- What changed and why (2 bullets)
- How to run locally (commands + sample payloads)
- Tests added/modified (unit/e2e)
- Risk and rollback plan (feature-flag off, quick revert commit)
- Owners to notify (QA/product)

ella: We have a QA team who wants a smoke scenario for manual verification — where do I place that?

eng-oncall: Add a "QA steps" section with concrete steps and expected responses. e.g.:
```
1) make dev
2) curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/exports -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"type":"async"}'
3) confirm job enqueued in redis via `redis-cli lrange exports:queue 0 -1`
```
Include screenshots or logs if helpful. QA will mark the PR with `qa-verified` once done.

ella: Nice. Anything about changelogs or contributors list? I added myself to AUTHORS.

frank: We don't require AUTHORS updates for every PR, but if you touch public APIs or add a user-visible feature, add a line in CHANGELOG/unreleased.md describing the user-facing change. AUTHORS is optional.

ci-helper: Tip: to nudge reviewers after a green CI, comment `@ci-helper forward` and the bot will ping pending CODEOWNERS after 10 minutes.

ella: One more: I ran `git range-diff` against origin/main after my rebase and there were subtle whitespace-only hunks. Any preferred way to bundle formatting fixes?

frank: If formatting changes are voluminous, create a separate PR `chore/format` that we can merge independently. For small formatting in your feature PR, keep them as isolated commit(s) with clear commit message. Use `git range-diff` in your comment if you want reviewers to see the before/after.

ella: If CI is green and reviewers LGTM, how quickly do PRs usually merge?

frank: Typically within 24 hours on working days. If you need faster turnaround add `priority:high` label and ping the on-call reviewer. For risky infra or release changes expect longer.

eng-oncall: Also note: if your change touches helm charts or k8s manifests add label `infra-review` and mention @infra-team. Those areas require explicit infra approval.

ella: Great — I'll add the checklist, separate the formatting commit, include QA steps, and mark ready. Thanks for the speedy help! :pray:

frank: Welcome again, and ping me for a quick pairing session on the rebase if you want.

ci-helper: automation: `pre-merge-checklist` passed locally? If yes, add comment `@ci-helper pre-merge ok` to help the merge queue prioritize.
